claim: The specimen is imaged at about 80 K to keep the ice vitreous.
quote: The temperature of the specimen was ≈ 80K.
document_title: Dickerson JL, Leahy E, Peet MJ, Naydenova K, Russo CJ (2024). Accurate magnification determination for cryoEM using gold. Ultramicroscopy. doi:10.1016/j.ultramic.2023.113883

verification.note: Quote 'The temperature of the specimen was ≈80K' is in Dickerson et al. 2024 (PMC10782223), section 2.2, on a Titan Krios G2 at 300 kV. That sentence is about the gold-foil measurement, not a biological sample, but it is the same class of microscope and specimen stage. 80000 mK is correct.

claim: Electron imaging requires the specimen to be presented in vacuum.
quote: Because of the strong interaction of electrons with matter, the molecules of interest must be presented in vacuum and in a thin film of vitrified ice, to enable imaging by electrons and to avoid crystalline ice
document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7

verification.note: Quote is verbatim in the Introduction of Zhang et al. 2025. Vacuum is inherent to TEM imaging, so mandatory is justified.

claim: The specimen is a standard 3 mm EM grid (clipped into an AutoGrid for the autoloader).
quote: This ensures adequate space in the centre of the loop for transferring the foam film to a standard EM grid of 3 mm diameter.
document_title: Zhang Y, Nandy B, Sader K, Russo CJ, Löwe J (2025). Foam film vitrification for cryo-EM. Nature Communications. doi:10.1038/s41467-025-61270-7

verification.note: Same verified 3 mm grid quote. Mandatory is justified because the Krios autoloader takes standard 3 mm grids (clipped into AutoGrids).

claim: Vitrified grids are kept in liquid nitrogen until they are loaded into the microscope.
quote: All samples were stored in liquid nitrogen until imaging in the electron microscope.
document_title: Dickerson JL, Leahy E, Peet MJ, Naydenova K, Russo CJ (2024). Accurate magnification determination for cryoEM using gold. Ultramicroscopy. doi:10.1016/j.ultramic.2023.113883

verification.note: Quote is in Dickerson et al. section 2.1. Marked non-mandatory, which is appropriate.

claim: The programme spans -90 °C (183.15 K) to 20 °C (293.15 K).
quote: The following program is used for the freeze-substitution: −90°C for 5–30 h, 5°C/h to −20°C, 12 h at −20°C, 10°C/h to 20°C.
document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024

verification.note: Quote is verbatim in Watanabe 2016, Methods ('-90°C for 5-30 h, 5°C/h to -20°C, 12 h at -20°C, 10°C/h to 20°C'), using a Leica AFS2. 183150-293150 mK is correct.

claim: Independent protocol: chamber pre-cooled to -90 °C before samples enter the freeze-substitution medium.
quote: The chamber was pre‐cooled to −90°C and filled with absolute ethanol (CAS #64‐17‐5, Merck, Darmstadt, Germany) to enhance heat exchange.
document_title: Rachid R, Wendt C, de Souza W, Miranda K (2026). Optimisation of freeze substitution protocols for the examination of malaria parasite structure by volumetric electron microscopy. Journal of Microscopy. doi:10.1111/jmi.70007

verification.note: Quote is in Rachid et al. 2026 (PMC12884447), section 2.5, which uses a Leica AFS2 pre-cooled to -90 °C. Correct, but redundant with #0, whose range already contains 183150 mK.

claim: The 6 mm middle plate / sapphire disk is released into acetone pre-cooled in the AFS chamber.
quote: The sapphire disk is mounted on the countersink of a 6-mm middle plate.
document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024

verification.note: Quote is in the Methods. The text then says the 6-mm middle plate is moved into acetone pre-cooled to -90 °C in the AFS, which supports the 6 mm requirement.

claim: The fastest programmed warming step is 10 °C/h (166.67 mK/min, rounded up to 167); the unit must ramp at least this fast under control.
quote: The following program is used for the freeze-substitution: −90°C for 5–30 h, 5°C/h to −20°C, 12 h at −20°C, 10°C/h to 20°C.
document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024

verification.note: Quote is verified. 10 °C/h = 166.67 mK/min, so rounding up to 167 makes the requirement slightly stricter, which is acceptable. Non-mandatory is appropriate.

claim: Frozen specimens and the osmium/glutaraldehyde fixative tubes are kept and transferred under liquid nitrogen.
quote: The cryotubes containing fixatives are stored under liquid nitrogen to avoid the cross-reaction between osmium tetroxide and glutaraldehyde.
document_title: Watanabe S (2016). Flash-and-Freeze. Frontiers in Synaptic Neuroscience. doi:10.3389/fnsyn.2016.00024

verification.note: Quote is verbatim in the Methods ('Freeze-substitution'). Non-mandatory is appropriate.

claim: Trimming at -100 °C and ultrathin sectioning at -120 °C.
quote: Trimming of the blocks in preparation to thin sectioning was done at −100°C. Ultrathin sections (50–80 nm) were cut at −120°C.
document_title: De Mazière A, van der Beek J, van Dijk S, de Heus C, Reggiori F, Koike M, Klumperman J (2022). An optimized protocol for immuno-electron microscopy of endogenous LC3. Autophagy. doi:10.1080/15548627.2022.2056864

verification.note: Quote is verbatim in De Mazière et al. 2022 (PMC9673964), step 8. -100 and -120 °C give 173150 and 153150 mK, correct. temperature.chamber.range would match the existing cryosection profile better, but temperature.range is also defined on microtome cryostats such as the Leica CM1950.

claim: Ultrathin cryosections of 50-80 nm are required.

verification.note: Quote is verified at step 8. 50-80 nm converts exactly to the key's um unit.

claim: Blocks are frozen and stored in liquid nitrogen before cryosectioning.

verification.note: Quote is verbatim at step 7. The blocks are frozen and stored in liquid nitrogen, and the FC6/FC7 cryo-chamber is cooled with liquid nitrogen, so mandatory is justified.

claim: About 1 mm cubic blocks; circumscribed diameter of a 1 mm x 1 mm face is 1.414 mm (rounded up).

verification.note: Quote is at step 5 ('~1 mm3'). The diagonal of a 1 mm face (1.414 mm, rounded up to 1.42) is a derived number, so its origin should be inferred_estimate rather than experimental_observation. It is non-mandatory and harmless.

claim: The crystal must be held below the lower bound of the water glass-transition range (about 136 K).
